Therefore, embedding campaign metadata fields as above, with strict length validation and no bulky blobs, aligns with current `/support` webhook payload capabilities without risking overflow or schema errors.

Please advise on next steps regarding Linear configuration. I will not submit or open any ticket until you explicitly instruct me to proceed given the current environment constraints.

Support schema: source enum defaults to from_bot when omitted; allowed values are from_user_triage, from_bot, from_github_issue, from_me.
Required fields: topic string and explanation string. Optional fields: imageUrl URL, sourceUrl URL/path, autoRepair boolean.
Parser: `/support source | topic | explanation | image-url`; if the first segment is not a valid source it becomes topic and source defaults to from_bot.
Validation: topic/explanation must be non-empty; imageUrl must be http/https; invalid image input becomes sourceUrl/path. Campaign tags are not supported today.
Payload risk: typical text payload is small; large screenshots are linked, not embedded. If campaign tags are added, cap count/length before Linear dispatch.
Hermes: ticket creation is separate from automation. Hermes should only act after the Linear ready label; logs/token metadata are outside chat context.

findings.title: Failure to submit approved support ticket despite explicit user confirmation
findings.description: In Turn 4, the user explicitly confirmed and requested the chatbot to submit a detailed ops support ticket with expanded parameters. Instead of submitting, the chatbot responded that the ticket was prepared but not created due to missing Linear configuration, effectively ignoring the user's explicit go-ahead and failing to proceed as requested. This breaks the expected operational flow and frustrates the user, who must now manually intervene or reconfigure the environment before audit can proceed.
findings.suggestedFix: Update chatbot logic to either submit the ticket as requested regardless of environment configuration or clearly prompt the user before the approval step that Linear configuration is mandatory. If the environment is not ready, the chatbot should explicitly ask the user to enable/configure Linear before approval, not silently block after approval.

findings.title: Chatbot fails to acknowledge or respond to user's explicit instructions in Turn 3
findings.description: After the user expanded the ticket request in Turn 3 with additional environment variables and DB schema requests, the chatbot responded with a generic environment limitations message repeating earlier disclaimers and did not confirm or acknowledge the expanded parameters. This shows loss of conversational context and failure to engage with the user's detailed instructions, reducing trust and usability.
findings.suggestedFix: Improve context tracking to recognize and confirm expanded or modified user requests, especially when users explicitly ask for confirmation before proceeding. The chatbot should paraphrase or confirm the updated parameters before waiting for further user input.

findings.title: Overly detailed and verbose audit summary in Turn 2
findings.description: The chatbot's response in Turn 2 is very long and dense, including many technical details, next steps, and hypothetical artifact lists. While thorough, it violates the product rule to keep answers concise and operational, potentially overwhelming the user and reducing clarity.
findings.suggestedFix: Condense audit summaries to focus on key actionable points and clearly separate what can be done now versus what requires additional input or tickets. Provide links or references for deeper details rather than embedding all information inline.

findings.title: Chatbot attempts to provide preliminary payload structure summary without full data access
findings.description: In Turn 5, the chatbot provides a detailed preliminary summary of payload size limits and campaign metadata alignment based on partial knowledge and user input. While helpful, this risks overstepping scope since the bot cannot verify exact schema or payload limits without logs or config files, potentially leading to inaccurate guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Clarify that preliminary summaries are best-effort and based on assumptions or user-provided data. Avoid detailed technical assertions without direct access to source data or logs, or clearly mark them as provisional.

findings.title: Reply under 30s
findings.description: Bot took 46552ms to respond, 1.6× the configured ceiling of 30000ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Investigate slow paths: token-count caps, retrieval latency, model choice. Consider streaming.
